uncertainties: Both 2027 syllabi are unpublished; flags follow the JEE Main 2026 (NTA) and JEE Advanced 2026 (IIT brochure) texts.

Flags are text-literal. Some basics that Advanced does not name (Kossel-Lewis, Fajans' rule, electrophiles/nucleophiles, electromeric effect, types of organic reactions, preparation of haloalkanes and alcohols, bond/atomisation enthalpies, catalyst effect on equilibrium) are marked Main-only, though coaching teaches them for Advanced anyway.

chem-surface-chemistry is listed Adv-only, but Main Unit 20 includes preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols; that one topic is flagged for both exams. The chapter-level Adv-only flag is otherwise correct.
Faraday's laws of electrolysis do not appear in the Main 2026 text (Unit 7), so that topic is Advanced-only.

Carboxylic acids: Main names only acidic strength, but the Unit 17 header ('general methods of preparation, properties, reactions and uses') covers all oxygen compounds, so preparation and reactions are flagged for Main too.

p-Block: Advanced's 'reactivity towards hydrogen, oxygen, halogens/acids/alkalis' for each group is folded into the group 'trends' topics, which are flagged for both because Main covers general trends in chemical properties. Named compounds are Advanced-only, except alums, since Main Unit 20 includes potash alum preparation.

Main Unit 20 placement: acid-base titrations and indicators go to ionic equilibrium; KMnO4 titrations go to redox (flagged both, since Advanced names redox stoichiometry); CuSO4 solution and neutralisation enthalpies go to thermodynamics; iodide/H2O2 kinetics goes to kinetics; Mohr's salt preparation goes to d-f block; potash alum goes to p-block 13-14; organic preparations (acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide, aniline yellow, iodoform) and functional-group tests go to practical organic; salt analysis goes to qualitative analysis.

Placement choices: concentration terms are in mole concept (Main lists them under Solutions, Advanced under General topics); lattice enthalpy is in chemical bonding (Main Unit 3; Advanced lists it under thermodynamics); aromaticity is in GOC; conformations are in isomerism (Main lists them under hydrocarbons); catalysis is in kinetics, following the Advanced text, not the old NCERT surface chemistry chapter.
Qualitative analysis ion lists differ: Ag+, Hg2+, Cr3+, Mn2+ and bicarbonate are Advanced-only; Ni2+, NH4+ and nitrite are Main-only.
Arrhenius acid-base concept is named only in Main, but is folded into a topic flagged for both. Trivial nomenclature (Main only) is folded into IUPAC nomenclature.
R,S and E,Z configurations and the benzyne mechanism are excluded by Advanced and absent from Main, so they are not listed as topics.
